title: A Preregistered Paired Evaluation of Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR) for Intent→Configuration NetOps: Null Results on a Synthetic Verifier-Checked Task Bank
abstract: We report a fully preregistered, archived paired experiment that tested whether a deterministic verifier plus a bounded LLM-guided repair loop (Generate–Verify–Repair, GVR) reduces verifier-detected semantic invariant violations for intent→device-configuration translation. Design: public synthetic NetOps task bank, N=240 paired tasks (12 clusters × 20 tasks), gpt-5-mini generator, pybatfish-style deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), shared_initial_candidate generation semantics (one generated candidate per task reused across arms), and at most one bounded repair attempt per task. Execution/accounting (artifact-backed): planned_episode_count=480, completed_episode_count=480, model_calls_used=240. Outcomes: every generated candidate satisfied the deterministic verifier in both arms (n11=240; n10=n01=n00=0). Paired estimate (rate_GVR − rate_baseline) = 0.0; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed=1729). Two preregistration→execution deviations materially constrain inference and are explicitly disclosed: (1) the executed shared-generation semantics violate the preregistered independent-per-condition generation assumption that underpinned the power calculation, and (2) a prespecified secondary primary comparison (GVR vs schema-constrained baseline) was not executed and no recorded rationale appears in the archive. Conservative conclusion: bounded GVR provided no verifier-detectable benefit under the executed semantics because there were no verifier-detectable errors to correct in this synthetic workload; results do not generalize beyond the specific model, prompt, task bank, verifier, repair budget, or generation semantics. We release authoritative archived artifacts (preregistration_sha256: eaedeae9aa302327e090d519a7a16f514d7fb79a472071aaf171f2f618c8ad4d) and recommend reproducible follow-ups (independent per-condition generation, adversarial/golden injections, multi-model runs, expanded verifier coverage).

sections.introduction:
Automating intent→device-configuration translation using large language models (LLMs) aims to reduce operator effort but poses safety risks: stochastic generators can emit syntactically plausible but semantically incorrect commands that violate operational invariants (reachability, workflow constraints, or security policies). A common engineering mitigation is to interpose deterministic validators and bounded repair loops—Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR)—so that mechanically checkable defects are detected and corrected before execution. However, empirical evidence quantifying the operational value of GVR under controlled, preregistered conditions is limited.

We conducted a fully preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment to answer a focused, operational research question: under a frozen design that used a single generator/prompt pairing and shared-initial-candidate generation semantics, does inserting a deterministic verifier plus a bounded LLM-guided repair loop reduce verifier-detected semantic invariant violations relative to an unconstrained baseline? The study, its preregistration, execution manifest, raw outputs, and analysis artifacts are archived and authoritative for all reported values (preregistration SHA-256: eaedeae9aa302327e090d519a7a16f514d7fb79a472071aaf171f2f618c8ad4d).

Contributions reported here: (1) a preregistered paired evaluation on a synthetic NetOps task bank (N=240 paired tasks) using gpt-5-mini and a pybatfish-style deterministic validator; (2) full execution accounting that documents shared_initial_candidate semantics (one generation per task reused across arms) and resource use (model_calls_used=240); (3) artifact-grounded confirmatory statistics showing a degenerate null outcome (n11=240, paired estimate=0.0, exact McNemar p=1.00, paired-bootstrap 95% CI=[0.0,0.0]); and (4) explicit disclosure of two preregistration→execution deviations that limit inference and concrete reproducible recommendations to restore discordance potential and test GVR under adversarial and multi-model regimes.
sections.related_work: Three near literatures motivate this study and frame its interpretation. First, broad surveys and empirical reports document LLM hallucinations and fabrication in code and structured-artifact generation, motivating deterministic validators in pipelines to reduce operational risk. Second, generate–verify–repair and constrained-decoding methods have been shown to improve syntactic and mechanically checkable properties (e.g., compilation, grammar validity) across code and domain-specific tasks; reported case studies indicate improved surface-level correctness but leave open semantic guarantees for domain invariants. Third, Network-Operations (NetOps) research emphasizes verifier-driven evaluation (reachability, policy invariants) and intent-based translation systems; many recent prototypes interpose validators and operator-approval workflows to mitigate risk. The supplied evidence map supports these claims and identifies open gaps: standardized semantic correctness benchmarks (G1), stronger LLM→formal-verifier integration (G2), and robustness under distribution shift (G3). The present experiment differs by being preregistered, paired, and artifact-archived; its null outcome under shared-generation semantics highlights how evaluation semantics condition measurable benefit.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimands: The study preregistration (study_id=c1_gvr_semantic_eval_prereg_v1) defined the primary estimand as paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (paired difference in verifier-detected semantic-violation rates). Two prespecified primary comparisons were registered: (C vs A) GVR vs unconstrained generation and (C vs B) GVR vs schema-constrained decoding; Bonferroni correction across the two comparisons (family alpha=0.05 → per-comparison alpha=0.025) was specified. The analysis executor 'paired_binary_analysis_v1' and all analysis rules were frozen prior to execution.

Design and frozen execution contract: Confirmatory sample N=240 tasks (12 topology/policy clusters × 20 tasks). Generator: requested gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Crucial frozen semantics recorded in the preregistration and manifest: generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (independent_condition_generation = false), initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1, maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1 (single bounded repair attempt), maximum_model_calls budget = 480, execution_mode = scientific_confirmatory. The preregistered power calculation targeted a 10-percentage-point absolute paired reduction with N=240 under an independent-per-condition generation assumption.

Task bank, oracle, and scoring: The public synthetic NetOps task bank encodes initial states, intent descriptions, workflow constraints, and expected final states; each task includes difficulty metadata and a canonical reference configuration. The deterministic validator implements pybatfish-style semantic checks and returns structured diagnostics (violation_count, violations list). Scoring rule: full_intent_constraint_validation as implemented by deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version 5.0). Representative per-task validator traces are archived and authoritative for scoring decisions.

Execution, missingness, and deviation handling: The preregistration specified exclusion and missingness rules ('complete_pair_primary'); technical failures would be logged and handled per these rules. The execution manifest records planned_episode_count=480, completed_episode_count=480, failed_episode_count=0, and model_calls_used=240. The manifest, raw results, and reconciliation artifacts are archived and authoritative (see execution_manifest and analysis artifacts). Two deviations that affect inference are explicitly disclosed and handled in analysis: (D1) the executed shared_initial_candidate generation semantics contradict the preregistered independent-generation assumption used in power planning; (D2) the prespecified comparison C vs B (GVR vs schema-constrained baseline) was not executed and no recorded rationale appears in the archive.
sections.results:
Execution accounting (artifact-backed): The execution manifest and deterministic reconciliation confirm planned_episode_count=480, completed_episode_count=480, failed_episode_count=0, complete_pair_count=240, and model_calls_used=240 under shared_initial_candidate semantics (one generation call per task reused across arms). Representative scoring artifacts (execution/scoring/*.json) show shared-initial candidate content identical to both arm responses for each task.

Primary confirmatory outcomes: Contingency table observed: n11=240 (both arms accepted), n10=0 (guarded only), n01=0 (baseline only), n00=0 (both rejected). Summary rates: baseline_success_rate=1.0; guarded_success_rate=1.0; paired estimate (rate_GVR − rate_baseline)=0.0. Exact McNemar two-sided p=1.00. Paired-bootstrap 95% CI (paired_bootstrap_percentile; bootstrap_resamples=10000; bootstrap_seed=1729) = [0.0, 0.0]. These results and the underlying CSV artifacts are archived (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; analysis/condition_summary.csv; analysis/analysis_log.jsonl) and are authoritative.

Repair activity and triggers: For every episode validator_trace.repair_applied=false; the bounded repair loop never executed because the shared-initial candidate satisfied the validator predicates for all tasks. contamination_summary.csv and missingness_summary.csv record zero flags and zero failures.

Statistical interpretation and degeneracy: The absence of any within-pair discordance (n10=n01=0) makes the paired estimate degenerate: there is no within-pair evidence that GVR could alter verifier outcomes under the executed semantics. The exact McNemar p=1.00 and bootstrap CI=[0.0,0.0] are deterministic consequences of this contingency given the preregistered analysis executor. Importantly, the preregistered power calculation assumed independent per-condition generation; because execution used shared_initial_candidate semantics (D1), the preregistered power argument does not apply to the observed run and cannot support claims of sensitivity to detect the prespecified 10-percentage-point effect.

Unexecuted prespecified comparison: The preregistration specified two primary comparisons (C vs A and C vs B). The archived execution artifacts document only the adapter-configured paired experiment comparing unconstrained baseline (A) to guarded GVR (C) under shared_initial_candidate semantics; the prespecified schema-constrained-baseline comparison (C vs B) was not executed and no recorded rationale for its omission appears in the archive. We treat this as a prespecified-but-unexecuted item and label it an unresolved procedural limitation in the inferential scope.
sections.discussion:
Conservative interpretation: Artifact-backed evidence shows bounded GVR provided no verifier-detectable benefit in this archived run because the generator+prompting pairing already produced verifier-acceptable outputs for every task. Two non-exclusive, artifact-supported mechanisms explain the null outcome. First, task/verifier alignment: the synthetic task bank, generator/prompt, and validator predicates defined a distribution the generator satisfied deterministically; the validator accepted the shared candidate in all cases. Second, sensitivity reduction from shared-generation semantics: reusing a single generated candidate across arms removes per-arm stochastic variation and therefore removes the within-pair discordance that GVR could exploit.

Implications for evaluation practice: To empirically measure GVR’s operational value it is necessary to restore discordance potential and verifier sensitivity. Recommended reproducible follow-ups, grounded in archived artifacts and preregistered plans, are: (R1) re-execute with independent per-condition generation (independent_condition_generation=true) using the archived task manifest and RNG seeds to restore paired stochasticity; (R2) inject adversarial or golden-reference tasks (the preregistration envisaged 10% golden tasks) to validate verifier sensitivity and prevent oracle complacency; (R3) expand generator scope beyond gpt-5-mini to measure cross-model generality; (R4) increase or permit iterative repair budgets and collect repair-iteration distributions; (R5) broaden verifier coverage (additional semantic invariants or formal-verifier hybrids) to reduce oracle incompleteness risk.

Threats to validity (artifact-grounded): Internal validity: the preregistration→execution mismatch (D1) invalidates the preregistered power calculation for the executed run; this is an internal-design risk. Construct validity: passing the deterministic validator does not guarantee absence of all operational hazards outside the verifier’s encoded invariants. External validity: single synthetic task bank, single model (gpt-5-mini), single bounded repair budget, and a single verifier limit generalizability. Conclusion validity: zero discordant outcomes preclude evidence for efficacy under the executed semantics. All of these threats are documented in the archived manifest and analysis artifacts and constrain claim scope.

Relation to prior work: The null outcome aligns with the broader literature's nuance: verifier-interposed pipelines reduce mechanically checkable errors, but measurable benefit depends on evaluation semantics, verifier completeness, task hardness, and generator stochasticity. Our preregistered paired design—when executed with independent per-condition generation and adversarial tasks—remains an appropriate route to quantify GVR's practical value.
sections.conclusion:
We executed a fully preregistered, artifact-archived paired experiment evaluating a bounded GVR intervention on a synthetic intent→configuration NetOps task bank. Under the executed shared-initial-candidate semantics, every generated candidate satisfied the deterministic validator in both arms (n11=240), yielding a degenerate null paired estimate (0.0), exact McNemar p=1.00, and paired-bootstrap 95% CI=[0.0,0.0]. Conservatively interpreted, bounded GVR did not add verifier-detectable value in this specific setting because there were no verifier-detectable errors to correct. Two prespecified deviations limit inference: the executed shared-generation semantics invalidated the preregistered independent-generation power assumption, and a prespecified schema-constrained-baseline comparison (C vs B) was not executed with no recorded rationale. We therefore avoid generalization beyond the specific model, prompt, task bank, verifier, repair budget, and generation semantics. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived and authoritative (preregistration_sha256: eaedeae9aa302327e090d519a7a16f514d7fb79a472071aaf171f2f618c8ad4d); we provide concrete reproducible next steps to evaluate GVR under conditions that restore discordance potential and adversarial sensitivity.

Acknowledgement: The complete artifact bundle, execution manifest, and analysis outputs are archived and available as the authoritative record accompanying this paper (see disclosure).

limitations: Synthetic task bank and verifier scope: N = 240 tasks were synthetic and evaluated against a pybatfish-style deterministic validator; results may not generalize to production topologies, vendor-specific syntax, or semantic invariants not encoded in the verifier.

Shared-generation semantics: the archived run used generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one initial generation per task reused across arms). This design reduced model-call cost but also removed per-arm stochastic variation and therefore reduced sensitivity to detect GVR benefits that rely on independent per-condition generator variability; the preregistered power calculation assumed independent per-condition generation and therefore does not apply to the executed design.
Single-model evaluation: the experiment used one generator (gpt-5-mini); cross-model generality is not established.
Repair budget: only a single bounded repair iteration was permitted; different or larger repair budgets or iterative strategies might produce different outcomes.
Verifier completeness risk: passing the deterministic verifier does not guarantee absence of all operational risks (unobserved invariants or properties outside the verifier model).

Prespecified comparison not executed: the preregistration included a prespecified schema-constrained-baseline comparison (C vs B) that was not executed in the archived run; the artifacts do not record a rationale, which is an unresolved procedural limitation.
